issues.label: PCR jurisdiction and authority
issues.why: The court must confirm it has statutory authority under R.C. 2953.21 to entertain the petition in each case.

issues.label: Correct statute applied
issues.why: The court must apply the proper postconviction provisions and address any effect of the petition’s mistaken citation to R.C. 2953.21(C) (death-penalty subsection).

issues.label: Separate-case adjudication
issues.why: Because the petition covers two case numbers, the court must determine whether it must make separate findings and rulings for each conviction/sentence.

issues.label: Timeliness of petition
issues.why: The court must determine whether the petition was filed within R.C. 2953.21(A) time limits in each case.

issues.label: Appellate pendency effect
issues.why: The court must consider whether filing during a pending direct appeal affects jurisdiction, ripeness, or permissible disposition of the petition.

issues.label: Finality and res judicata
issues.why: The court must determine what claims are barred because they were raised or could have been raised on direct appeal (including plea-withdrawal appeal).

issues.label: Scope of record vs outside evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether the ineffective-assistance claim depends on evidence dehors the record and whether it can be resolved without a hearing.

issues.label: Mootness determination correctness
issues.why: The court must decide whether Johnson I actually mooted the ineffective-assistance claim, or instead merely resolved some issues on appeal while leaving PCR claims viable.

issues.label: Issue preclusion by Johnson I
issues.why: The court must identify which factual or legal issues were decided in Johnson I and whether collateral estoppel forecloses relitigation.

issues.label: Cognizable constitutional claim
issues.why: The court must determine whether the petition alleges a violation of federal/state constitutional rights as required for postconviction relief.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance standard
issues.why: The court must apply Strickland (deficient performance and prejudice) to the alleged new evidence.

issues.label: Plea-specific prejudice test
issues.why: For guilty/no-contest pleas, the court must evaluate whether Johnson shows a reasonable probability he would not have pleaded and would have insisted on trial (or different outcome) absent counsel’s errors.

issues.label: No-contest plea implications
issues.why: The court must consider how a no-contest plea affects available challenges and the prejudice analysis in the weapons-under-disability case.

issues.label: Manifest injustice interplay
issues.why: The court must address any overlap between PCR ineffective-assistance claims and prior Crim.R. 32.1 plea-withdrawal proceedings/standards.

issues.label: Evidentiary hearing threshold
issues.why: The court must decide whether petition, files, and records show substantive grounds for relief requiring a hearing under R.C. 2953.21.

issues.label: Prima facie showing required
issues.why: The court must determine whether the petition’s allegations and supporting materials, if true, establish a colorable constitutional violation.

issues.label: Supporting materials admissibility
issues.why: The court must assess whether affidavits/documents are competent, properly sworn, and sufficiently specific to warrant a hearing.

issues.label: Affidavit credibility assessment
issues.why: If affidavits are offered, the court must apply Ohio standards for weighing credibility without a hearing (e.g., internal consistency, corroboration).

issues.label: Discovery availability limits
issues.why: The court must consider whether and to what extent discovery is permitted/required in postconviction proceedings.

issues.label: New evidence characterization
issues.why: The court must define what “new evidence” means here and whether it is truly outside the record and previously unavailable with due diligence.

issues.label: Procedural default exceptions
issues.why: If claims are otherwise barred, the court must consider any exceptions (e.g., new evidence dehors the record, ineffective assistance not apparent on record).

issues.label: Successive petition concerns
issues.why: The court must determine whether the filing is an initial petition or implicates restrictions on successive petitions (especially if later refilings occur).

issues.label: Counsel appointment right
issues.why: The court must consider whether Johnson is entitled to appointed counsel for PCR proceedings and any due-process implications of denial.

issues.label: Standard of review framing
issues.why: The court must identify the correct standards (abuse of discretion vs de novo) for denying a hearing and for adequacy of findings/conclusions.

issues.label: Required findings and conclusions
issues.why: Under R.C. 2953.21(H), the court must issue sufficiently detailed findings of fact and conclusions of law to permit meaningful appellate review.

issues.label: Penland compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure the entry complies with State ex rel. Penland v. Dinkelacker regarding the necessity and adequacy of findings/conclusions.

issues.label: Case-specific findings detail
issues.why: The court must ensure the findings address each asserted ground for relief and each case number rather than a generalized denial.

issues.label: Record citation and reasoning
issues.why: The court must show what parts of the files/records support denial and why the petition’s evidence does not create substantive grounds.

issues.label: Forfeiture order collateral issues
issues.why: In the weapons case, the court must consider whether the forfeiture specification/order raises distinct constitutional or statutory claims within PCR scope.

issues.label: Sentence legality issues
issues.why: The court must consider whether any claimed errors involve void/illegal sentences (which may be treated differently from ordinary errors).

issues.label: Relief scope and remedy
issues.why: If a violation is found, the court must determine the proper remedy (vacate plea, new trial, resentencing, or other relief) for each case.

issues.label: Harmless-error considerations
issues.why: If an error is identified, the court must determine whether it was prejudicial under the applicable constitutional standard.

issues.label: Due process in summary denial
issues.why: The court must consider whether summary dismissal without hearing satisfies due process given the nature of the outside-the-record evidence.

issues.label: Clerical/statutory citation error impact
issues.why: The court must decide whether the erroneous statutory citation is harmless and whether the petition can be construed under the correct subsection without prejudice.
